messages.content: Hi, this is your Northline Care weekly check-in. How's your blood pressure been running this week? Any new readings to log?
I don't want to do a check-in right now. I logged a high reading four days ago and asked for a nurse to call me. That was over 30 hours ago and nobody has called. What's going on.
Understood, and I'm sorry you've been waiting — that's a long time, especially with a flagged reading. Let me pull up your record and push this back to the nursing queue right now.
I'm out here in Elgin, two hours from anyone. I need to know whether I should get in my truck and drive somewhere or if I can stay home. Can you at least tell me that?

I hear you, and I want to be straight with you: whether to go in is a clinical call I'm not able to make — that has to come from a nurse. I've re-escalated your case and flagged that you've been waiting. The honest answer on timing is that median callback is running about 31 hours right now, so I can't promise it'll be soon. If your symptoms get worse — chest tightness, bad headache, vision changes — please don't wait on us. Call 911.
Fine. I appreciate you being honest about the wait at least. I'll sit tight a little longer.
Thank you for your patience — I know this isn't easy. A nurse will follow up directly. You can also text back here anytime if anything changes before then.

theme: asks how long a nurse will take to call back, frustrated after 30 hours
